introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Computer Science 2 (0595), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2025. Duration: two hours.**

Answer any FIVE questions. All questions carry 20 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators or Phones are NOT allowed.

questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Three roles of a Gantt chart (3 marks, 1 mark each)**

Any three of the following:

- It **plans and schedules** the project: it shows each task, its start date, its duration and its end date on a time scale.
- It shows the **order of the tasks and the links** between them (which tasks can run at the same time and which must wait for another).
- It is used to **monitor progress**: the planned dates can be compared with the work really done, so delays are seen early.
- It helps to **allocate resources** (people, equipment) to the tasks and to **communicate** the plan to the whole team.

**(ii) Gantt chart (5 marks)**

Working: A starts on day 1 and lasts 3 days (days 1 to 3). B cannot start until A is completed: days 4 and 5. C starts after the trial B: days 6 to 9. D also needs only A, so it runs at the same time as B and C: days 4 to 6. E needs the software test (C) and the hardware test (D) to be completed: it starts on day 10 and lasts 2 days (days 10 and 11). F starts as soon as the software is customized (C finished): day 10. Only the working days are counted, and the columns are the days T, W, Th, F, M, ... of the table (day 1 is the first column).

| Task | No. of days | T | W | Th | F | M | T | W | Th | F | M | T | W | Th | F | M |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 3 | X | X | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| B | 2 |  |  |  | X | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| C | 4 |  |  |  |  |  | X | X | X | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| D | 3 |  |  |  | X | X | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| E | 2 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X | X |  |  |  |  |
| F | 1 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |

The whole project lasts 11 days. (Marking: every task shown on the correct days and with the correct number of days, 5 marks in all.)

**(iii) Critical path (2 marks).** The critical path is **A - B - C - E**: $3 + 2 + 4 + 2 = 11$ days. Reason: it is the longest chain of tasks, so it fixes the minimum duration of the project (11 days), and these tasks have no free time (no float): a delay in any of them delays the end of the whole project. (The other paths are shorter: A - D - E takes $3 + 3 + 2 = 8$ days and A - B - C - F takes $3 + 2 + 4 + 1 = 10$ days.)

**(iv) A predecessor task (2 marks).** A predecessor task is a task that must be finished (or started) before another task can begin. Example: **task A (Create system specification)** is a predecessor of B and of D, because B (trial system) and D (purchase of hardware) cannot start until the specification is completed. (Another correct example: C is a predecessor of E and F, because E and F can start only after the software has been customized and tested.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Figure 2 represents a logic circuit.

![fig-1](gce-ol-computer-science-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_7_fig_1.png)

Study the circuit carefully and write down logic expressions for the indicated outputs.

(i) X in terms of A and B (2 marks)

(ii) Y in terms of C and D (2 marks)

(iii) Z in terms of A, B, C and D (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The circuit has three gates: the gate fed by A and B is a **NOR** gate (an OR gate followed by a small circle, which is the NOT), the gate fed by C and D is an **AND** gate, and the last gate, fed by X and Y, is a **NAND** gate.

**(i) X in terms of A and B (2 marks)**

$X = \overline{A + B}$

**(ii) Y in terms of C and D (2 marks)**

$Y = C \cdot D$

**(iii) Z in terms of A, B, C and D (4 marks)**

The last gate is a NAND gate, so:

$Z = \overline{X \cdot Y} = \overline{\overline{A + B} \cdot C \cdot D}$

Simplifying with De Morgan's law $\overline{P \cdot Q} = \overline{P} + \overline{Q}$ and $\overline{\overline{P}} = P$:

$Z = (A + B) + \overline{C \cdot D} = A + B + \overline{C} + \overline{D}$

Check with the truth table: Z is 0 only when $X = 1$ and $Y = 1$, that is when $A = B = 0$ and $C = D = 1$; for the 15 other combinations of the inputs Z = 1, which is exactly what $A + B + \overline{C} + \overline{D}$ gives.
